mainEntity.name: How do I find my appliance's wattage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check the nameplate on the back or underside. If it lists volts and amps, multiply them to get watts. For devices that cycle, such as refrigerators and air conditioners, a plug-in power meter shows real use over time.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between peak and off-peak rates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Time-of-use plans charge more when demand is high, often late afternoon and evening, and less overnight. Running an EV charger, dishwasher or dryer off-peak can cut its cost noticeably if your plan has these tiers.

Energy in kWh is multiplied by an emissions factor for the grid. The US average is roughly 0.37 kg of CO₂ per kWh, while the marginal or non-baseload rate is higher at about 0.5 kg. Cleaner grids are much lower. Edit the factor to match your area.

mainEntity.name: Why does a 1,500 W heater not use 1.5 kWh every hour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Thermostats switch the heating element off once the room reaches the target temperature. If it runs 30 minutes in an hour, it uses 0.75 kWh. The calculator assumes constant use unless you reduce the hours.
A kilowatt-hour is the energy used by a 1,000 watt device running for one hour. It is the unit your electricity bill is based on.
